usage:
From C:/Users/DWP2/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Users-DWP2-Desktop-Project-walkthrough/e1e2f8a1-5b17-462a-bbe8-01925d989674/scratchpad/p0/detector:
  python openings.py mappings/<drawing>.json <out.json> [--png <dir>]
e.g. python openings.py mappings/bank1.json output/bank1_openings.json --png output
It finds tools/prims.py by walking up from the script folder, loads the cache named in the mapping, writes {"openings": [...]} and one PNG per floor (openings_<floor>.png: doors red, windows blue, passages green, ids labelled, '?' = eitherKind, wall solid grey). Output fields: id, floor, kind, subtype, a, b (wall centre line, drawing metres), width, wallThickness, host (wall|glass|none), hinge (a|b|null), swing (left|right of a->b, null when unknown), confidence, evidence (rules fired, layers), eitherKind.
Scoring: python work/score_safe.py ../keys/final/all.json output/all_openings.json [--only sukhumvit,presidential] [--out x.json]. score_safe.py runs the UNMODIFIED tools/score.py on a copy of the key with "eitherKind": false added where missing, because score.py crashes otherwise (see notes). work/dev_all.py runs all four drawings and scores them in one go; work/crop.py <drawing> <area> x0,y0,x1,y1 draws a review crop with the key overlaid. The blind-run code is frozen in frozen_v1/ (same command line).

rules.name: 1 Wall solid
rules.what: Wall/column-layer fills, thin closed outlines (mean width <= 0.35 m) and face lines paired 4-45 cm apart, continuous linetypes only; cracks and corner squares closed. Wider closed outlines (room outlines) and pieces under 0.15 m are not walls.
rules.catches: The base for every gap; drops room-outline polylines on wall layers (E291, the presidential toilet outline) and dashed overhead lines.

rules.name: 2 Strip-end gaps
rules.what: Wall strips = pairs of opposite faces of the wall solid. From every strip end look along its centre line for the next wall material; the stretch is a gap, typed by near end (cap / L-corner / T) and far end (end of a collinear strip of the same thickness, or the face of a wall).
rules.catches: Locator for most doors, windows and passages, including corner-ended gaps (GW-05, GW-14, UW-06, UW-07, O1-O6) that end-cap pairing misses.

rules.name: 3 Swing arcs
rules.what: Arcs on any layer and linetype (r 0.28-2 m, sweep 20-125 deg). Closed vs open end from a leaf (line or thin rectangle, any non-wall layer, tolerant of 3-point arcs off the hinge) and from the closed tip lying on the wall.
rules.catches: Door symbols on DOOR, 0, WALL, WIN, A-DOOR, xref and Vietnamese door layers, HIDDEN arcs, partial sweeps (43-61 deg).

rules.name: 4 Swings in gaps
rules.what: Each arc goes to the gap that fits it best (greedy by score); leaves must cover >= 55% of the gap. Two leaves with meeting closed tips = double door, also when drawn in front of a deep reveal (offset <= 1 m, same span). If the wall gap is much wider than the leaves, ends move to jambs beside them.
rules.catches: Single, double, pivot and 3-leaf doors; UW-09 (double door drawn 0.7 m in front of its partition); D1 (gap 2.09 m narrowed to the 1.6 m jambs).

rules.name: 5 Doors from the symbol alone
rules.what: Arc + leaf in no gap: wall band from sections beside the chord, ends snapped to wall ends, glazing or jambs (small closed shapes on any layer, outer faces of 50 mm frames, inner faces of wall-sized stubs) within 0.35 m; else the chord. Glass doors in glass screens and arc pairs with nothing to bound them are dropped.
rules.catches: Walls drawn through (GW-08, GE-11), undrawn wall (D14), facade door on a dimensions layer (D15), door in a glazed screen (GE-06), UE-18.

rules.name: 6 Casement windows
rules.what: Sashes (arcs not on a door layer) in a gap whose glazing is drawn across the whole gap in the closed position, or over glass drawn inside a drawn-through wall, are windows.
rules.catches: UE-03, UE-05, UE-06, UE-07 (outward sashes on WIN); keeps curtain-wall doors (arc on A-DOOR) as doors (B1-09).

rules.name: 7 Glazing bands
rules.what: Parallel lines on window/glass layers grouped into bands; a band in a gap glazes it. Units split fixed vs sliding (25 mm track spacing / shifting panels) only between two units >= 2 m. Fixed -> window; sliding -> window (eitherKind) unless it opens straight onto a hatched floor with no planting, then a sliding glass door.
rules.catches: Windows in gaps and bays; GE-01 (fixed pane) vs GE-19 (sliding door); GW-20, GW-21 (sliding doors onto the deck); UW-14 stays a window (planted roof).

rules.name: 8 Bays, corners, glass walls
rules.what: A band in no gap is a bay when wall ends/columns bound it within 0.25 m, including a post-less glass corner (end on the other band's line). Rejected as glass walls: glass-layer screens running from one cross wall to another, one side of an all-glass corridor (parallel band 0.8-3.5 m away, similar length >= 2.5 m), runs over 7 m.
rules.catches: GW-01, GW-07, UW-05, UE-20, UW-16/UW-17 corner; rejects the glazed link sides, shower screens, pool glass.

rules.name: 9 Glass inside a drawn-through wall
rules.what: A band inside the wall solid: the opening is where the wall is thinner over the glass (free stretch along the missing strip) or between jambs at the glass ends.

rules.name: 10 Sliding, pocket and lift doors
rules.what: In a gap: a thin panel (15-70 mm) running into a wall pocket, a centre-line leaf slid part-way out of a pocket on one side, or a leaf drawn shut across the gap on a door layer. Outside gaps: a panel half out of a pocket where the wall simply ends, running to the next wall or to the line of a second pocket door met at a corner. Swing leaves are never read as panels.
rules.catches: UW-11, UW-12, UW-13, GE-09, D7, lift doors B1-05 and B2-22.

rules.name: 11 Frame-only and low-wall openings
rules.what: Both wall faces drawn on across a gap between two wall ends (continuous, non-outline lines) = opening over a low wall (window); >= 2 frame pieces standing inside a gap, or >= 3 edge-aligned frame pieces in a row from one wall face to another with no wall between = frame-only sliding unit (window).

rules.name: 12 Passages
rules.what: Empty gap accepted only if: both ends wall ends of one wall line (<= 3.6 m, <= 2.5 m from an L-corner, and the line carries on past the far end), or a wall end to a wall face that carries on (<= 1.6 m); not stub to stub, not at a free-standing post (squarish, <= 0.9 m, nothing within 0.15 m), not across a stair, wall >= 7 cm, building on both sides.
rules.catches: All 18 scored passages; rejects carport posts, pilasters, kerbs, stair ends, 5 cm cladding lines.

rules.name: 13 Fusion
rules.what: Parallel overlapping detections on one wall line are merged; door > window > passage, then confidence, then far-end type, then wall thickness.
rules.catches: Both faces of a wall, two leaves of a double wall, gap + symbol duplicates, duplicated blocks.

perDrawingConfig: Each mappings/<drawing>.json holds only the four things staff confirm: "cache" (which prims cache), "units" ("mm"), "floors" (area -> floor name), and "layers" (role -> list of layer names; roles used: wall, column, glass, window, door, stair, ignore). There are no coordinates, handles, thresholds, block names or exception lists. sukhumvit: wall 3, column 1, glass 1, window 3, door 5, stair 1, ignore 16 layers (furniture, fixtures, grid, dimensions, text, site; TREE left unmapped). presidential: wall 1, column 1, door 2, ignore 21. bank1/bank2: wall A-WALL, A-WALL-PATT; column S-COLS; glass A-GLAZ-CURT, A-GLAZ-CWMG; door A-DOOR, A-DOOR-FRAM, A-DOOR-GLAZ, A-DOOR-HDLN; stair S-STRS, S-STRS-MBND; ignore 16 annotation, furniture, casework, services and grid layers. The bank mappings were written once, from the layer names and the overview PNGs, at the blind run (14:10) and never changed afterwards. The code has no layer names, block names or coordinates in it: it checks only the role sets and generic geometry.

notes:
Process: development on sukhumvit and presidential, first against the provisional key, then against final parts as they appeared, then the final key. The code was frozen in detector/frozen_v1 at 14:09. The bank mappings were written once from layer names and the overview PNGs. The blind run happened at 14:10, and I scored it once before looking at any bank key file or bank geometry. Its result is 39/41 (0.951) on both the provisional and the final key; the only misses were the two lift doors read as window/passage. The improvement rounds after that worked on all five floors with general rules:
(1) lift doors (a leaf drawn shut on a door layer), and passages between two stubs rejected;
(2) after the final u-east part arrived: casement windows, glazed-corridor glass walls, and a looser leaf finder for 3-point arcs;
(3) frame-only rows, swing leaves never read as sliding panels, and a free-post size limit.
Every floor's RIGHT is now at least 0.90, so I stopped.

Scorer bug: tools/score.py crashes ('TypeError: int += NoneType' at line 79) whenever a matched pair has different classes and the key item has no eitherKind field. In the final key 168 of 170 items have no such field. The cause is that c_ok = (...) or (k.get('eitherKind') and ...) evaluates to None instead of False; wrapping it in bool() would fix it. I did not modify score.py. work/score_safe.py runs the unmodified script on a key copy with eitherKind: false added, which changes no score.

Kind caveats: sliding sashes without paving outside are output as windows with eitherKind true, because the plan cannot show sills. Door vs passage confusions are counted right by the scorer; none remain in the final output.

The final key changed a lot from the provisional one. For example, the WIN-layer sash sets UE-05/06/07 became casement windows, U-P09/U-P10 were rejected, and the sliding units GW-19/20/21 and GE-19 became doors. The frozen v1 therefore scores 0.902 on the dev floors against the final key, against 0.982 on the provisional key.

Nothing was deployed or published. Everything is in the scratchpad detector folder.
